description: Test your knowledge of PA H8 | Lymphadenopathy & Lymphomas.

cards.text: Define lymphadenopathy in adults. What are the size thresholds for normal vs abnormal nodes?
cards.answer: Lymphadenopathy is node enlargement >1 cm in any axis. Exception: inguinal nodes up to 1.5 cm are normal; epitrochlear nodes >0.5 cm are abnormal.

tip.tip: Remember 1 cm rule for most nodes, but epitrochlear is half that (0.5 cm).

cards.text: What are 'B symptoms' in lymphoma staging and why are they clinically significant?
cards.answer: B symptoms = fever, night sweats, weight loss. They significantly raise malignancy suspicion and indicate systemic disease rather than reactive lymphadenopathy.

tip.tip: B = Systemic symptoms; B symptoms = Bad sign for malignancy risk.

cards.text: What is the duration threshold for persistent unexplained lymphadenopathy that mandates biopsy?
cards.answer: Persistent lymphadenopathy >6 weeks without obvious cause requires biopsy to rule out malignancy.

tip.tip: 6 weeks = time to stop waiting and start investigating.

cards.text: Describe follicular hyperplasia: compartment, morphology, and key aetiology.
cards.answer: Follicular hyperplasia occurs in the cortex (B-cell zone) with enlarged germinal centres and tingible-body macrophages. Caused by B-cell stimulation (RA, SLE, early HIV, Toxoplasma, bacterial infections).

tip.tip: Follicular = B-zone = germinal centre action; tingible-bodies = immune activity marker.

cards.text: Describe paracortical hyperplasia: compartment, morphology, and key aetiology.
cards.answer: Paracortical hyperplasia expands the T-cell zone with activated immunoblasts. Follicles compressed/absent. Caused by T-cell stimulation (EBV, CMV, phenytoin, vaccinations).

tip.tip: Paracortical = T-zone; Think EBV-infected mononucleosis as classic example.

cards.text: How do you distinguish follicular lymphoma from follicular hyperplasia histologically?
cards.answer: Follicular lymphoma lacks tingible-body macrophages and shows bcl-2 positivity, whereas follicular hyperplasia retains normal tingible-bodies and germinal centre architecture.

tip.tip: Tingible-bodies = sign of normality; bcl-2+ = sign of malignancy.

cards.text: What are the classic features of Hodgkin lymphoma that distinguish it clinically from reactive nodes?
cards.answer: Hodgkin lymphoma presents with rubbery, non-tender nodes (often mediastinal), bimodal age peaks (15–34, >55), and frequently accompanied by B symptoms.

tip.tip: Hodgkin = Rubbery + bimodal peaks + mediastinal love.

cards.text: Name three infectious causes of reactive lymphadenopathy: one bacterial, one mycobacterial, one viral.
cards.answer: Bacterial: Staphylococcus/Streptococcus (pyogenic, tender); Mycobacterial: tuberculous (matted, caseating); Viral: EBV (generalised, posterior cervical in mononucleosis).

tip.tip: Pyogenic = tender & fluctuant; TB = matted & cascading; EBV = sore throat sign.
